title: Bathroom Remodeling Software: 6 Tools for Trades, Photos, Pay
html:
Bathroom remodeling software should track the lead, schedule the trades and prove the hidden work. Zoho CRM has a free edition for the lead list, Jobber and Housecall Pro schedule visits and invoices, and CompanyCam keeps the photo record. Published plans run from $12 to $299 a month before extra users.

Bathroom remodeling software has to handle a fast job with many hands on it. A bath remodel can last days instead of weeks, but it still needs a plumber, a tile setter, an electrician and a final clean. This guide sorts six tools by the step they handle, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit.

Bathroom jobs hide their riskiest work behind a wall. Waterproofing, pipe fittings and wiring are covered by tile and drywall within days. A tool that records those steps with photos protects you later. A tool that books the trades in the right order protects the schedule now.

Which tool keeps bathroom remodeling leads in one list?

Zoho CRM has a free edition that is enough to log bathroom leads for a small team. It is a general tool, so you add the bathroom fields yourself.

  • Zoho CRM: a deal pipeline with custom fields and reports. The Free edition covers up to 3 users. Limit: Free allows 10 custom email templates, 10 data exports and 5,000 API calls a day, and its paid prices appear in your local currency, so check the vendor for a dollar figure.

Add the fields a bath job needs: tub or shower, size of the room, budget range, timeline and whether it is a one-bath or whole-house project. Add a field for accessibility needs, because a walk-in shower or grab bars change the scope and the price.

Keep the stages short: new, visited, quoted, booked, completed and lost. A homeowner who asked for a quote and heard nothing for three days has probably hired someone else.

Which software schedules bathroom crews and subcontractors?

Jobber and Housecall Pro both schedule visits and send invoices. They are strongest when a bath job is a series of short appointments.

  • Jobber: scheduling, quotes, invoices and online payments. Core for one user is $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 a month billed annually, and Connect for one user is $139 a month with no commitment. Limit: extra users cost $29 a month each, and card payments carry a 2.9% plus 30 cents fee.
  • Housecall Pro: Basic is $59 a month billed annually for one user, or $79 billed monthly. Essentials is $149 billed annually for 5 users, and Max is $299 billed annually for 8 users with extra users at $35 a month. Limit: Pipeline, Payroll, Voice and Websites are listed as add-ons without prices.

Order matters more than speed in a bathroom. Demo comes first, then rough plumbing and electrical, then inspection, waterproofing, tile, fixtures and the final clean. If the tile setter arrives before the waterproofing cures, you pay twice. Build the order into a job template so every bath starts with the same sequence.

Subcontractors need clear visit windows and addresses. Ask each vendor how a sub sees an assignment, whether that costs a paid user, and what the customer receives as a reminder. Housecall Pro lists $35 for each extra user on Max, and Jobber lists $29, so a crew with many subs can add up quickly.

Which tool proves hidden bathroom work with photos?

CompanyCam is a photo and documentation tool, and it earns its keep in bathrooms because so much work gets covered.

  • CompanyCam: its site describes photo and video capture with unlimited cloud storage, annotations, project timelines, checklists, reports and integrations with QuickBooks and Jobber. Core is $63 a month, Crew is $129 and Scale is $199, all billed annually, with extra users at $29 a month each. Limit: Core includes 10 AI credits and 5-minute videos, and the page lists no free plan.

Use a photo checklist for every bath: the room before demo, the open walls, the rough plumbing, the waterproofing, the tile layout and the finished room. Six photos per job take five minutes. They answer a leak complaint months later without a return visit.

ToolJob it doesPublished priceReal limit
Zoho CRMLead list and pipelineFree for 3 usersPrices in local currency
JobberScheduling and invoices$49 monthly, $29 annual$29 per extra user
Housecall ProScheduling and dispatch$59 annual, $79 monthlyAdd-ons unpriced
JoistEstimates and invoices$12 to $32 a month5 documents on Basics
CompanyCamJob photos and reports$63 to $199, billed annuallyAI credits capped on Core
QuickBooksAccounting$38 to $140 a monthPromo ends after 3 months

Prices checked on each vendor page in November 2026. Annual prices are per month billed yearly.

Which tools handle bathroom remodeling estimates, deposits and the books?

Joist handles estimates and invoices, and QuickBooks handles accounting. A bathroom job usually needs a deposit up front, so the payment step matters.

  • Joist: estimates, invoices and online payments for small contractors. Basics is $12 a month billed monthly, Pro is $17, Elite is $32 and Run is $100. Limit: Basics allows 5 documents a month, and the free plan is no longer offered.
  • QuickBooks: invoicing, bank feeds and reports. Simple Start is $38 a month, Essentials is $85 and Plus is $140, with promotional prices for the first three months. Limit: the free tier allows 2 invoices a month and 1 bank connection.

A deposit schedule keeps cash ahead of costs. Many bath remodelers collect a deposit at signing, a payment at rough-in and a final payment at completion. Whatever schedule you choose, write it into the estimate and ask each tool how it handles a partial invoice.

What does one bathroom remodel look like in software?

One bath touches every tool in the stack. Walk a single job through it before you buy.

  • Inquiry: a homeowner calls or submits a form, and the lead goes into the list the same day.
  • Visit and estimate: you measure, photograph the room and send a priced estimate with a deposit line.
  • Scheduling: demo, plumbing, electrical, waterproofing, tile and fixtures are booked in order.
  • Production: the crew photographs each stage before it is covered.
  • Punch list: a short checklist closes small issues before final payment.
  • Invoice and review: the final invoice goes out on completion, with a review request the same week.

If a tool cannot carry the job through all six steps without retyping, plan for a second tool to fill the gap, and decide who owns each step.

What does a bathroom remodeling software stack cost?

A small bath remodeler can start at about $12 a month and reach roughly $300. The ranges below use only published prices.

  • Lean: Zoho CRM Free, Joist Basics at $12 a month and QuickBooks Simple Start at $38. Cost: $50 a month plus card fees.
  • Middle: Jobber Core at $49 a month month to month, CompanyCam Core at $63 a month billed annually and QuickBooks Simple Start at $38. Cost: $150 a month before extra users.
  • Crew-based: Housecall Pro Essentials at $149 a month billed annually for 5 users, plus CompanyCam Crew at $129 a month billed annually. Cost: $278 a month.

Compare each total with the profit on one average bath. If a tool saves one callback or one missed deposit a quarter, it has likely paid for itself. If nobody opens it, cancel it.

How should a bathroom remodeler plan the trade order in software?

Build one job template per bath type, with the trades in order and a duration for each. A template turns a new job into a ten minute task instead of an hour.

  • Demo and haul-away: one day for a standard bath, and a dumpster or haul slot booked with it.
  • Rough plumbing and electrical: booked in the same window so inspection can follow.
  • Inspection and waterproofing: a photo checkpoint before anything covers the walls or the floor.
  • Tile and grout: scheduled only after the waterproofing has cured as the product label says.
  • Fixtures, glass and paint: last, with the final clean and punch list at the end.

Ask the vendor how a delayed step moves the rest of the schedule. In a bathroom, one late plumber pushes tile, glass and the customer move-in date. A tool that shifts the dependent visits for you saves a day of phone calls, and one that does not leaves it to you.

Keep a short buffer after inspection. Inspectors rarely arrive when you want them, and a crew standing idle costs more than a day of slack. Build that buffer into the template and tell the homeowner at signing, so a delay is not a surprise.

What mistakes do bathroom remodelers make with software?

Most regrets come from buying for a bigger company than you run. Four mistakes show up most often.

  • Skipping the photo step: the one job without a waterproofing photo is the one that gets a leak complaint.
  • Paying for users who never log in: subs often need only a schedule view, so ask what a view-only user costs.
  • No pilot job: a demo bath hides the awkward steps. Run one real job through the tool before committing.
  • No owner: pick one person to enter costs, upload photos and close out jobs. Shared ownership usually means no ownership.

Training is part of the price. Give your crew leads ten minutes to learn the photo app on a live job, and show them what it saves them, such as fewer callbacks. A tool that crews resent will stay empty.

How do you choose bathroom remodeling software?

Choose bathroom remodeling software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it schedule trades in order, hold a deposit schedule and store photos by stage?

Cost: add the plan, extra users for subs, card fees and add-ons, then compare against the profit on one average bath.

Setup effort: can you build a bath job template and import customers in one weekend?

A solo remodeler fits the lean stack. A company with a few crews and many subs fits Housecall Pro or Jobber with CompanyCam. Pilot one live bath before you move every job, and keep the old process running beside it for a week.

What software does a bathroom remodeler need?

A bathroom remodeler needs a lead tracker, a scheduling tool for the trades, a way to send estimates and take deposits, and a photo record of hidden work. Start with the step that loses you the most money, then add the rest as jobs grow.

How much does bathroom remodeling software cost?

Published prices in this guide run from free for Zoho CRM to $299 a month for Housecall Pro Max billed annually. Joist starts at $12 a month billed monthly. Extra users, card fees and add-ons cost more, so a small stack can land between $50 and $300 a month.

Is Jobber or Housecall Pro better for a bathroom remodeler?

Both schedule visits, send quotes and take payments. Jobber lists Core for one user at $49 a month with no commitment. Housecall Pro lists Basic for one user at $59 a month billed annually. Test both with a real bathroom job and compare the extra user costs.

Do bathroom remodelers need photo software?

It is worth considering, because waterproofing, pipes and wiring are covered quickly. Photos protect you in a leak or warranty dispute. CompanyCam lists Core at $63 a month billed annually, which you can compare against the cost of one return visit.

Is there a free CRM for bathroom remodeling?

Yes. Zoho CRM lists a Free edition for up to 3 users, with limits of 10 custom email templates, 10 data exports and 5,000 API calls a day. Check those limits before you rely on it for your whole pipeline, and ask about paid prices in your currency.

How should bathroom remodelers collect deposits?

Write a deposit schedule into the estimate, such as a deposit at signing, a payment at rough-in and a final payment at completion. Joist and QuickBooks both send invoices, so ask how each handles a partial payment and what card fees apply.

How do bathroom remodelers get more leads?

Most leads come from local search, a clear website and reviews, not from project software. Complete your Google Business Profile, post finished baths and ask for a review after each job. Search ads can add volume once your crew has room for more work.

How should a bathroom remodeler plan the trade order in software?
Build one job template per bath type, with the trades in order and a duration for each. A template turns a new job into a ten minute task instead of an hour.
-
Demo and haul-away:
one day for a standard bath, and a dumpster or haul slot booked with it.
-
Rough plumbing and electrical:
booked in the same window so inspection can follow.
-
Inspection and waterproofing:
a photo checkpoint before anything covers the walls or the floor.
-
Tile and grout:
scheduled only after the waterproofing has cured as the product label says.
-
Fixtures, glass and paint:
last, with the final clean and punch list at the end.
Ask the vendor how a delayed step moves the rest of the schedule. In a bathroom, one late plumber pushes tile, glass and the customer move-in date. A tool that shifts the dependent visits for you saves a day of phone calls, and one that does not leaves it to you.
Keep a short buffer after inspection. Inspectors rarely arrive when you want them, and a crew standing idle costs more than a day of slack. Build that buffer into the template and tell the homeowner at signing, so a delay is not a surprise.
##
What mistakes do bathroom remodelers make with software?
Most regrets come from buying for a bigger company than you run. Four mistakes show up most often.
-
Skipping the photo step:
the one job without a waterproofing photo is the one that gets a leak complaint.
-
Paying for users who never log in:
subs often need only a schedule view, so ask what a view-only user costs.
-
No pilot job:
a demo bath hides the awkward steps. Run one real job through the tool before committing.
-
No owner:
pick one person to enter costs, upload photos and close out jobs. Shared ownership usually means no ownership.
Training is part of the price. Give your crew leads ten minutes to learn the photo app on a live job, and show them what it saves them, such as fewer callbacks. A tool that crews resent will stay empty.

How do you choose bathroom remodeling software?
Choose bathroom remodeling software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.
Fit:
does it schedule trades in order, hold a deposit schedule and store photos by stage?
Cost:
add the plan, extra users for subs, card fees and add-ons, then compare against the profit on one average bath.
Setup effort:
can you build a bath job template and import customers in one weekend?
A solo remodeler fits the lean stack. A company with a few crews and many subs fits Housecall Pro or Jobber with CompanyCam. Pilot one live bath before you move every job, and keep the old process running beside it for a week.
###
What software does a bathroom remodeler need?
A bathroom remodeler needs a lead tracker, a scheduling tool for the trades, a way to send estimates and take deposits, and a photo record of hidden work. Start with the step that loses you the most money, then add the rest as jobs grow.
###
How much does bathroom remodeling software cost?
Published prices in this guide run from free for Zoho CRM to $299 a month for Housecall Pro Max billed annually. Joist starts at $12 a month billed monthly. Extra users, card fees and add-ons cost more, so a small stack can land between $50 and $300 a month.
###
Is Jobber or Housecall Pro better for a bathroom remodeler?
Both schedule visits, send quotes and take payments. Jobber lists Core for one user at $49 a month with no commitment. Housecall Pro lists Basic for one user at $59 a month billed annually. Test both with a real bathroom job and compare the extra user costs.
###
Do bathroom remodelers need photo software?
It is worth considering, because waterproofing, pipes and wiring are covered quickly. Photos protect you in a leak or warranty dispute. CompanyCam lists Core at $63 a month billed annually, which you can compare against the cost of one return visit.
###
Is there a free CRM for bathroom remodeling?
Yes. Zoho CRM lists a Free edition for up to 3 users, with limits of 10 custom email templates, 10 data exports and 5,000 API calls a day. Check those limits before you rely on it for your whole pipeline, and ask about paid prices in your currency.
###
How should bathroom remodelers collect deposits?
Write a deposit schedule into the estimate, such as a deposit at signing, a payment at rough-in and a final payment at completion. Joist and QuickBooks both send invoices, so ask how each handles a partial payment and what card fees apply.
###
How do bathroom remodelers get more leads?
Most leads come from local search, a clear website and reviews, not from project software. Complete your Google Business Profile, post finished baths and ask for a review after each job. Search ads can add volume once your crew has room for more work.
